title: Posterior Default Network Modulation in Alcohol Use Disorder
official: Posterior Default Network Modulation in Alcohol Use Disorder
summary: This proposal will test whether repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) modulation of the brain's posterior default mode network (pDMN) will alter alcohol craving, alcohol seeking and impulsivity in men and women who have an alcohol use disorder but are not seeking treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Men and women aged 21 - 55
* Alcohol Use Disorder diagnostic criteria based on Interview, Screening, and Measures of at least moderate severity
* ≥7 or 14 drinks/week average over the last month or ≥ 3 or 4 drinks/occasion for women and men respectively
* Positive alcohol cue reactivity screening
* Systematic Delay Discounting behavior
* Right-handed

Exclusion Criteria:

* Physical Exam, Vital Signs, Electrocardiogram, Laboratory Values, or screening assessment precluding safe participation or experimental procedures
* Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol (CIWA) 177 ≥8 or reported significant risk symptoms
* MRI contraindications
* Pregnant or breast-feeding women; Women who do not attest to using accepted forms of birth control
* Current or desire for AUD or substance use treatment
* Medical conditions (e.g., seizure disorder) that may influence participant safety or study outcome)
* Positive urine drug screen for amphetamines/ methamphetamines, barbiturates, benzodiazepines, cocaine, opiates, or phencyclidine and evidence of intoxication
* Medications or dosage changes (past 30 days) that could influence participant safety or data (e.g., antidepressants, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, etc.) or interact with alcohol
* Current/history of neurological disease of cerebral origin, head injury with \> 20 min loss of consciousness, medical treatment impacting MRI data, or serious psychiatric illness (bipolar disorder, psychosis).
* Positive BrAC reading precluding visit completion
* Actively suicidal or are at serious suicidal risk
* Left-handed or ambidextrous
* First degree family member with seizure disorder
* Inability to understand English study instructions
* Intoxication from any substance terminates an experimental day and will be considered for overall exclusion or study participation.
